text.p: Fidelity Investments said Friday that Abigail Johnson, daughter of Chairman Ned Johnson, will give up managing mutual funds to take up new responsibilities within the company.

Johnson was named group leader for the Specialized Growth Group of mutual funds and, in a separate role, will also represent the fund managers in the development of new technology systems, Fidelity said.

She had been manager of the $1.3 billion Fidelity Trend Fund since June, 1996, which returned 7.92 percent during her tenure vs. 16.75 percent for the S&P 500 up until Thursday, according to Morningstar Inc.
Johnson has headed six funds including Trend Fund since joining Fidelity full-time as a manager in 1988 after earning an MBA degree from Harvard University.

"Given the increasing amount of information and reasearch we're managing, and the more than $50 million we spend on technology for investment professionals, I am pleased to have Abby overseeing this important venture," William Hayes, chief operating officer for equity investments said in a statement.
Johnson succeeds William Danoff as head of the Growth Group. Danoff chose to focus exclusively on managing the $23.8 billion Fidelity Contrafund and the Fideility VIP Fund II: Contrafund.
In addition, Bart Grenier was promoted to assistant equity division head to assist Hayes in the management of the group, including overseeing research, portfolio management and trading functions.
Arieh Coll was named manager of Fidelity Trend Fund, scceeding Johnson. Coll previously managed the $400 million Fidelity Export Fund.

Jason Weiner was named manger of the Export Fund. He previously managed the Fidelity Select Computers Portfilio and was an analyst following retail office products, personal computers and workstations.
To replace Weiner, Fidelity named Michael Tempero to manage Select Computers. He will continue to manage Fidelity Select Insurance Portfolio.
Separately, Fidelity will introduce a few more index funds in addition to the three it already offers.
"We'll be adding more index funds," spokeswoman Robyn Tice said. She declined to be more specific.
The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that Fidelity will introduce three index funds.
